   "source": [
    "# Elevation and cycling\n",
    "\n",
    "This notebook adds heights and grades to a walk graph, makes walking times depend on the slope, and builds a bike graph with its level of traffic stress. Heights normally come from a raster file (`add_elevation(graph, \"dem.tif\")`, which needs `pip install \"iduedu[elevation]\"`). So that the notebook runs anywhere, it uses a hill of 60 m defined as a function of the coordinates; Vasilyevsky Island itself is flat."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "22d82306",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T18:26:46.842530Z",

    }

   "source": [
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "\n",
    "import iduedu\n",
    "\n",
    "walk = iduedu.get_walk_graph(osm_id=OSM_ID, clip_by_territory=True)\n",
    "centre = walk.nodes_gdf.geometry.union_all().centroid\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def hill(x, y):\n",
    "    \"\"\"A hill of 60 m with a radius of about 400 m in the middle of the island.\"\"\"\n",
    "    return 60 * np.exp(-((x - centre.x) ** 2 + (y - centre.y) ** 2) / (2 * 400**2))\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "walk = iduedu.add_elevation(walk, hill)\n",
    "walk.edges_gdf[['length_meter', 'grade', 'grade_max', 'ascent', 'descent']].describe().round(3)"
   ]
  },

   "cell_type": "code",

    "    ax.set_axis_off()"
   ]

   "source": [
    "## Walking times on slopes\n",
    "\n",
    "`apply_grade_speed` divides the time of every edge by the relative speed of a model. Tobler's hiking function is fastest on a gentle descent of 5 %. The flat times stay in `time_min_flat`."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "edf41d8c",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-11-10T18:26:50.580128Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-11-10T18:26:50.580128Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-11-10T18:26:50.620446Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-11-10T18:26:50.619942Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "flat ground: 44.3 min, with the hill: 45.2 min\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "hilly = iduedu.apply_grade_speed(walk, 'tobler')\n",
    "\n",
    "xs, ys = hilly.nodes_gdf.geometry.x, hilly.nodes_gdf.geometry.y\n",
    "west = ((xs - (centre.x - 1500)) ** 2 + (ys - centre.y) ** 2).idxmin()\n",
    "east = ((xs - (centre.x + 1500)) ** 2 + (ys - centre.y) ** 2).idxmin()\n",
    "\n",
    "flat_cost, flat_route = iduedu.shortest_path(hilly, west, east, weight='time_min_flat')\n",
    "hill_cost, hill_route = iduedu.shortest_path(hilly, west, east, weight='time_min')\n",
    "print(f'flat ground: {flat_cost:.1f} min, with the hill: {hill_cost:.1f} min')"
   ]
  },

   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,

    "basemap(ax, hilly, 'The fastest walk across the hill')\n",
    "hilly.path_to_edges(flat_route, weight='time_min_flat').plot(ax=ax, color=BLUE, linewidth=2.5, label='flat ground')\n",
    "hilly.path_to_edges(hill_route, weight='time_min').plot(ax=ax, color=ORANGE, linewidth=2.5, label='Tobler')\n",
    "ax.legend()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]

   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "`max_lts=2` keeps the network that most adults are willing to ride, and `keep_largest_subgraph` (the default) its largest strongly connected component: the part where every place can be reached from every other without riding in heavy traffic. Compare it with all the edges up to level 2."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 10,
   "id": "4bd90587",
   "metadata": {

    }
   },
   "outputs": [

     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "all ways: 442 km, edges up to LTS 2: 356 km, of them connected in both directions: 30 km\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "low_stress = iduedu.get_bike_graph(osm_id=OSM_ID, clip_by_territory=True, max_lts=2)\n",
    "pieces = iduedu.get_bike_graph(osm_id=OSM_ID, clip_by_territory=True, max_lts=2, keep_largest_subgraph=False)\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def km(graph):\n",
    "    return graph.edges_gdf['length_meter'].sum() / 1000\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f'all ways: {km(bike):.0f} km, edges up to LTS 2: {km(pieces):.0f} km, '\n",
    "      f'of them connected in both directions: {km(low_stress):.0f} km')"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "7428a3ab",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Most edges up to level 2 here are service roads inside the blocks. The streets between them are secondary and tertiary roads with `maxspeed=RU:urban`, which is not a number, so they take the default of 60 km/h for their class, the urban limit in Russia, and reach level 4. The low-stress edges therefore fall into many small pieces: even with the direction ignored, the largest piece holds 2 692 of the 13 644 nodes. Cycle lanes mapped on those streets would join them."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "6f1cb785",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Heights from a raster\n",
    "\n",
    "With a digital elevation model the call is the same, and the raster may be in any CRS:\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "walk = iduedu.add_elevation(walk, \"dem.tif\")\n",
    "walk = iduedu.apply_grade_speed(walk, \"tobler\")\n",
    "bike = iduedu.get_bike_graph(osm_id=OSM_ID, elevation=\"dem.tif\")\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "Global models such as Copernicus GLO-30 measure roofs and trees in cities; use a terrain model for street grades. Spot heights and contour lines in a GeoDataFrame work as well (`column=` names the height column)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "55c2380e",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Your own area\n",
    "\n",
    "Replace `OSM_ID` with the id of an OSM boundary relation, or pass `territory=` a shapely polygon in EPSG:4326 or a\n",
    "GeoDataFrame. Measures near the border of a graph are biased, because the network beyond it is missing: build the\n",
    "graph for a larger area and pass the study area as `area=` to `graph_stats` and `centrality`. For many runs on one\n",
    "region, read a local OSM file instead of Overpass with `iduedu.use_pbf(...)` (see the data sources page)."
   ]
  }
 ],
